text:
The Panthers got what they wanted in the summer, Brady Tkachuk alongside his brother, and the brothers are delivering the way they always have: loud and effective. With Sam Bennett between them, the Tkachuks get 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five. Their father has been booed in Toronto and has taken aim at Senators fans over Brady's exit, which tells you how personal that trade still feels in Ottawa.

Florida sits 10-7-2 with a 56% chance at the playoffs in our simulations. The process is better than the record: 53% of the chances, and about five fewer goals than those chances earned. Aaron Ekblad and Gustav Forsling are the clearest example, with 62% of the expected goals and a minus five goal differential anyway.

No team in this group lives in the penalty box like Florida. They take 5.7 penalties a game and draw 5.8, and their power play creates more than a goal of expected offense a night. It's a fun way to play and a volatile one.

The worry is depth. Sandis Vilmanis was hurt on a Tom Wilson boarding hit that got Wilson ejected and drew no further discipline, a ruling Florida media has not taken quietly. Anton Lundell has been day to day, and the Lundell line with Vilmanis has been their best at limiting chances. What to watch: how that line holds up while it's broken.
headline: Two Tkachuks, a lot of penalties
